requirements.original: A break statement causes the exit from a loop, from an altstep or from an alt or interleave statement.
requirements.canonical: A `break` statement SHALL cause the exit from a loop, from an altstep, or from an `alt` or `interleave` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- A break statement causes the exit from a loop, from an altstep or from an alt or interleave statement.

requirements.original: break
requirements.canonical: The `break` statement has the syntax `break`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- break

requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a formal parameter identifier as a log item.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

requirements.original: On executing a break statement the innermost, currently executed loop, alt statement or interleave statement is left.
requirements.canonical: On executing a `break` statement, the innermost, currently executed loop, `alt` statement or `interleave` statement SHALL be left.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- On executing a break statement the innermost, currently executed loop, alt statement or interleave statement is left.

requirements.original: Execution continues with the statement following the construct which is left.
requirements.canonical: After a `break` statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the construct which is left.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- Execution continues with the statement following the construct which is left.

requirements.original: Using break outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) or an alternative of an alt or interleave statement shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside the body of a loop (`for`, `while`, `do-while`) or an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement; such use SHALL cause an error.

readings: A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside a loop body, an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement, or a top alternative of an altstep; misuse is detected at compile time.
A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside a loop body or an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement (altsteps excluded); misuse causes a runtime error.
ambiguity.issue: The list omits altsteps although 19.12-s001 and 19.12-s018 allow break in a top alternative of an altstep, and it does not say whether the error is a compile-time or runtime error; chosen reading: break in altstep top alternatives is allowed and misuse is a static error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- Using break outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) or an alternative of an alt or interleave statement shall cause an error.

requirements.original: If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep (see clause 16.2.1) ends with a break statement, the altstep and the surrounding alt statement are left.
requirements.canonical: If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep ends with a `break` statement, the altstep and the surrounding `alt` statement SHALL be left.
requirements.condition: the execution of a top alternative of an altstep ends with a break statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep (see clause 16.2.1) ends with a break statement, the altstep and the surrounding alt statement are left.

requirements.original: Execution continues with the statement following the surrounding alt statement.
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is left by a `break` statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the surrounding `alt` statement.
requirements.condition: an altstep is left by a break statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- Execution continues with the statement following the surrounding alt statement.

requirements.original: These statement blocks are not executed when the altstep is left by executing a break statement.
requirements.canonical: An optional statement block following an altstep call in an `alt` statement IS NOT executed when the altstep is left by executing a `break` statement.
requirements.condition: the altstep is left by a break statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- These statement blocks are not executed when the altstep is left by executing a break statement.

requirements.original: A return statement has to be used, if such an optional statement block has to be executed (see clause 19.10).
requirements.canonical: If the optional statement block following an altstep call has to be executed, the altstep SHALL be left with a `return` statement.
requirements.condition: the optional statement block following the altstep call has to be executed
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.12 -- A return statement has to be used, if such an optional statement block has to be executed (see clause 19.10).

requirements.original: A continue statement causes the start of the next iteration of a loop.
requirements.canonical: A `continue` statement SHALL cause the start of the next iteration of a loop.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.13 -- A continue statement causes the start of the next iteration of a loop.

requirements.original: continue
requirements.canonical: The `continue` statement has the syntax `continue`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.13 -- continue

requirements.original: On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.
requirements.canonical: On executing a `continue` statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop SHALL be skipped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.13 -- On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.

requirements.original: On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.
requirements.canonical: On executing a `continue` statement, the next iteration of the innermost, currently executed loop SHALL start.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.13 -- On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.

requirements.original: Using continue outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: A `continue` statement SHALL NOT be used outside the body of a loop (`for`, `while`, `do-while`); such use SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.13 -- Using continue outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) shall cause an error.

requirements.original: Statement blocks can be used like basic program statements to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.
requirements.canonical: A statement block MAY be used like a basic program statement to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.14 -- Statement blocks can be used like basic program statements to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.

requirements.original: The declarations and statements in a statement block are executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially.
requirements.canonical: The declarations and statements in a statement block SHALL be executed sequentially in the order of their appearance.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.14 -- The declarations and statements in a statement block are executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially.

requirements.original: "{" { LocalDefinition | Statement } "}"
requirements.canonical: A statement block has the syntax "{" followed by any number of LocalDefinition or Statement elements followed by "}".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.14 -- "{" { LocalDefinition | Statement } "}"

requirements.original: A statement block defines a local scope unit.
requirements.canonical: A statement block IS a local scope unit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.14 -- A statement block defines a local scope unit.

requirements.original: An interleaving operator allows the specification of interleaved sequences or alternatives.
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement CAN specify interleaved sequences or alternatives.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 20 and table 19 call the construct the interleave statement; 'interleaving operator' is used only here.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- An interleaving operator allows the specification of interleaved sequences or alternatives.

requirements.original: Alternative behaviour; Col2: alt { … }
requirements.canonical: Alternative behaviour IS expressed with the `alt` statement, written `alt { … }`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- Alternative behaviour; Col2: alt { … }

requirements.original: Re-evaluation of alt statements; Col2: repeat
requirements.canonical: Re-evaluation of an `alt` statement IS expressed with the `repeat` statement, written `repeat`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- Re-evaluation of alt statements; Col2: repeat

requirements.original: Interleaved behaviour; Col2: interleave { … }
requirements.canonical: Interleaved behaviour IS expressed with the `interleave` statement, written `interleave { … }`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- Interleaved behaviour; Col2: interleave { … }

requirements.original: Activate a default; Col2: activate
requirements.canonical: A default IS activated with the `activate` operation, using the keyword `activate`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- Activate a default; Col2: activate

requirements.original: Deactivate a default; Col2: deactivate
requirements.canonical: A default IS deactivated with the `deactivate` operation, using the keyword `deactivate`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.0 -- Deactivate a default; Col2: deactivate

requirements.original: When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement is entered, a snapshot IS taken.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.

requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean guards of the alternative branches.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all relevant stopped test components.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all relevant timeout events.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in at least one alternative of the `alt` statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in a top alternative of an altstep invoked as an alternative in the `alt` statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in a top alternative of an altstep activated as a default IS relevant for the snapshot.

readings: A test component, timer or port referenced in a top alternative of any altstep that is currently activated as a default IS relevant for the snapshot.
A test component, timer or port referenced in a top alternative of an altstep activated as a default within the alt statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'activated as default' is unclear (activated anywhere vs. within the alt statement); chose the first reading, because defaults are activated outside the alt statement and are appended to every alt.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.1 -- Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

requirements.original: alt [ @nodefault ] "{" { ( VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) [";"] } { "[" [ BooleanExpression ] "]" ( ( TimeoutStatement | ReceiveStatement | TriggerStatement | GetCallStatement | CatchStatement | CheckStatement | GetReplyStatement | DoneStatement | KilledStatement ) StatementBlock ) | ( AltstepInstance [ StatementBlock ] ) } [ "[" else "]" StatementBlock ] "}"
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement has the syntax `alt` [`@nodefault`] "{" followed by optional local variable, timer, constant or template definitions, followed by alternatives of the form "[" [BooleanExpression] "]" with either a timeout, receive, trigger, getcall, catch, check, getreply, done or killed statement followed by a statement block, or an altstep instance followed by an optional statement block, and an optional final "[" `else` "]" StatementBlock, closed by "}".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- alt [ @nodefault ] "{" { ( VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) [";"] } { "[" [ BooleanExpression ] "]" ( ( TimeoutStatement | ReceiveStatement | TriggerStatement | GetCallStatement | CatchStatement | CheckStatement | GetReplyStatement | DoneStatement | KilledStatement ) StatementBlock ) | ( AltstepInstance [ StatementBlock ] ) } [ "[" else "]" StatementBlock ] "}"

requirements.original: An alt statement may define some local definitions before its alternative branches.
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement MAY define local definitions before its alternative branches.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- An alt statement may define some local definitions before its alternative branches.

requirements.original: These can be used by all the branches.
requirements.canonical: A local definition of an `alt` statement CAN be used by all branches of that `alt` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- These can be used by all the branches.

requirements.original: When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement is entered, a snapshot IS taken.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.

requirements.original: If the alt statement contains local definitions before its first branch, these are evaluated before the snapshot is taken.
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains local definitions before its first branch, the local definitions ARE evaluated before the snapshot is taken.
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains local definitions
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- If the alt statement contains local definitions before its first branch, these are evaluated before the snapshot is taken.

requirements.original: When the alt statements executes the repeat operation, the whole alt statement, including the local definitions, is re-evaluated.
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement executes the `repeat` operation, the whole `alt` statement, including its local definitions, IS re-evaluated.
requirements.condition: a repeat statement is executed in the alt statement

ambiguity.issue: "repeat operation" is used, while clause 20.3 names it the repeat statement; also "alt statements executes" is grammatically garbled.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- When the alt statements executes the repeat operation, the whole alt statement, including the local definitions, is re-evaluated.

requirements.original: The alternative branches in the alt statement and the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and altsteps that are activated as defaults are processed in the order of their appearance.
requirements.canonical: The alternative branches of an `alt` statement, the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and the top alternatives of altsteps activated as defaults ARE processed in the order of their appearance.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The alternative branches in the alt statement and the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and altsteps that are activated as defaults are processed in the order of their appearance.

requirements.original: If several defaults are active, the reverse order of their activation determines the evaluation order of the top alternatives in the defaults.
requirements.canonical: If several defaults are active, the top alternatives of the defaults ARE evaluated in the reverse order of the activation of the defaults.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- If several defaults are active, the reverse order of their activation determines the evaluation order of the top alternatives in the defaults.

requirements.original: If the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this alt statement.
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives ARE ignored for the execution of that `alt` statement.
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- If the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this alt statement.

requirements.original: Else-branches are always chosen and executed when they are reached (see below).
requirements.canonical: An else-branch IS always chosen and executed when it is reached.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- Else-branches are always chosen and executed when they are reached (see below).

requirements.original: The` evaluation of the Boolean guards shall be based on the snapshot.
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean guard SHALL be based on the snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The` evaluation of the Boolean guards shall be based on the snapshot.

requirements.original: The Boolean guard is considered to be fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined, or if the Boolean guard evaluates to true.
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard IS considered fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined or if the Boolean guard evaluates to `true`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The Boolean guard is considered to be fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined, or if the Boolean guard evaluates to true.

requirements.original: An altstep-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled.
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- An altstep-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled.

requirements.original: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, i.e. the altstep is invoked and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.
requirements.canonical: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, i.e. the altstep is invoked and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.

requirements.original: An altstep-branch may contain an optional statement block.
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch MAY contain an optional statement block.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- An altstep-branch may contain an optional statement block.

requirements.original: The optional statement block shall be executed only, if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.
requirements.canonical: The optional statement block of an altstep-branch SHALL be executed only if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The optional statement block shall be executed only, if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.

requirements.original: A done-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.
requirements.canonical: A done-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the stopped list of the snapshot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- A done-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.

requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the done operation.
requirements.canonical: The selection of a done-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `done` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the done operation.

requirements.original: The done operation itself has no further effect.
requirements.canonical: A `done` operation in a selected done-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The done operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.original: A killed-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.
requirements.canonical: A killed-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the killed list of the snapshot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- A killed-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.

requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the killed operation.
requirements.canonical: The selection of a killed-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `killed` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the killed operation.

requirements.original: The killed operation itself has no further effect.
requirements.canonical: A `killed` operation in a selected killed-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The killed operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.original: A timeout-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.
requirements.canonical: A timeout-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- A timeout-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.

requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the specified timeout operation, i.e. removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the timeout operation.
requirements.canonical: The selection of a timeout-branch causes the execution of the specified `timeout` operation, i.e. the removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the `timeout` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The selection causes execution of the specified timeout operation, i.e. removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the timeout operation.

requirements.original: A receiving-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the matching criteria of receiving operation is fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.
requirements.canonical: A receiving-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria of the receiving operation are fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria are fulfilled
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- A receiving-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the matching criteria of receiving operation is fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.

requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the receiving operation, i.e. removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, maybe an assignment of the received information to a variable and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.
requirements.canonical: The selection of a receiving-branch causes the execution of the receiving operation, i.e. the removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, possibly an assignment of the received information to a variable, and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- The selection causes execution of the receiving operation, i.e. removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, maybe an assignment of the received information to a variable and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.

requirements.original: In the case of the trigger operation the top message of the queue is also removed if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria is not.
requirements.canonical: In a receiving-branch with a `trigger` operation, the top message of the port queue IS removed also if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria are not.
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria of the trigger operation are not
requirements.header: // @requirement: 20.2 -- In the case of the trigger operation the top message of the queue is also removed if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria is not.
